get_case.description: Read the full record of one decided case: its name, the day it was decided, every way it can be cited, the judges who sat on it, how often it has been cited since, and whatever the court published alongside the decision such as the syllabus, the posture and the procedural history. It also lists the separate decisions written in the case, so the majority, a concurrence and a dissent can each be read in full with Get a decision. Takes the case ID that a case law search or a citation check returned.

case.case_name_full: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
case.syllabus: Segregation of children in public schools solely on the basis of race deprives children of the minority group of equal educational opportunities.

get_decision.description: Read the words of one decision in full: a majority opinion, a concurrence, a dissent or a per curiam order. The answer says which kind it is, who wrote it, which judges joined it, and which other decisions it cites, and carries the text itself with the markup taken off, ready to summarise, quote or search in a later step. Takes the decision ID that a case law search or Get a case returned.

decision.text: We come then to the question presented: Does segregation of children in public schools solely on the basis of race, even though the physical facilities and other tangible factors may be equal, deprive the children of the minority group of equal educational opportunities? We believe that it does.

get_federal_case.description: Read the full record of one federal court case: its name and docket number, the court and the judge, when it was filed, when anything was last filed in it, whether it has been closed, what kind of suit it is, and what it was appealed from. It also points at the decisions published in the case and any recorded oral arguments, so the litigation and the case law it produced join up. Takes the case ID that a federal case search returned.

look_up_citations.description: Find every case citation in a piece of text and check each one against the archive. Paste in a brief, a memo, a contract or anything a language model wrote, and get back each citation it contains with a verdict: the real case it points to, or a plain statement that no such case exists. Citations with a typo in them are corrected where the correction is obvious. This is the step to put in front of anything that will be filed or sent, because an invented citation reads exactly like a real one until somebody looks it up.

description: Search American law in the free archive run by the nonprofit Free Law Project. Search around ten million published court decisions, federal and state, and read any of them in full. Check every case citation in a piece of writing against the archive, which is how an invented citation is caught before it is filed. Follow federal litigation through the dockets collected out of PACER, from the case down to what was filed and when. Look up the judges who decide these cases and every seat they have held, and find recorded oral arguments with the audio. Free to use, with a free account.
